text: "Take the kick out of the intro and bring the bass in" is step 4 of the approved AI-1 design, word for word. In Basic mode it remakes the whole bassline with new notes and does NOT bring the bass into the intro. Only the kick part works. Other ways of saying it do the same: "bring the bass in at the build" and "start the bass at the build" each remake the bassline across the whole song and change no sections (the second one also starts playback). So a comment about one section rewrites a part the user may already like. This breaks the 19 Nov owner rule. Only "bring the bass in IN the build" and "add the melody to the intro" work.
steps:
1. New song. Type "make a beat like Stephan Bodzin", then "add a bassline", "add some chords", "add a melody", then "make it a full track" (the Intro has only drums).
2. Type "take the kick out of the intro and bring the bass in".
Result: the reply is "Done: Bassline on Rolling Bass in A minor, Intro: kick out." The Bassline notes change (48 notes, new pattern), and the Bassline is still off in the Intro.
3. Undo. Type "bring the bass in at the build", then "start the bass at the build".
Result: both remake the bassline everywhere, and no section's parts change.
Should: switch the bass on in that section (Intro / Build), keep its notes, and reply with "Intro: bass in".
Likely: src/maker.js AI-1 parts parser (~lines 206-217). "bring X in" with no section after it, or with "at the <section>", falls through to add_bass. assistant-dev.

text: Asking to mute the voice note starts a NEW recording. "Mute the voice note" and "turn off the voice note" reply "Recording a voice note after the count-in: 4 bars", open the microphone and count in. "Mute sing" (the imported file's track name) starts a sung melody take. "Mute the recording" isn't understood. Only "mute the vocal" mutes it. So a mix request turns the mic on and records over the beat. The previous run left an extra "Voice note 1" track in the song.
steps:
1. New song: "make a beat like Stephan Bodzin", "add a bassline", "add some chords".
2. Import tests/fixtures/sing.wav (Import audio / MIDI). It becomes the audio track "sing".
3. Type "mute the voice note".
Result: "Done: Recording a voice note after the count-in: 4 bars." LOOP.state = counting, MIC.on = true, and the track isn't muted.
4. "turn off the voice note" does the same. "mute sing" gives "Sing the melody after the count-in". "mute the recording" gives "I couldn't turn that into a change".
Should: mute (or unmute) the audio track, and never start a take.
Likely: src/maker.js, where the sing / voice-note intent wins over mute/turn off when the sentence names "voice note" or a track called "sing". assistant-dev.

text: A comment that names a section changes the whole song, or nothing, and the reply doesn't say which. In Song mode: "the melody is too loud in the drop" turns the Melody down 5 dB in every section. "The bass is too loud in the intro" does the same for the bass. "Make the hats softer in the break" lowers the whole Drums fader (0.90 to 0.78), not the hats and not just the break. "Make the melody quieter in the break" sets the Melody volume for the whole song. "Make the build more intense" once rewrote the drum groove in every section (168 to 184 hits). Another time it, and also "give the drop more energy" and "more energy in the drop", replied "Done: Groove: …" while nothing in the song changed. "Make the drop bigger", "make the first drop bigger" and "make the drop huge" (named in the AI-1 release) get "I couldn't turn that into a change". "Make the drop hit harder" puts the drum compressor up everywhere. Nothing in the song can be changed for one section only, so Keys should at least say "in every section", or offer what it can do for that section (parts in/out, its own pattern).
steps:
1. New song: "make a beat like Ben Böhmer", "add a bassline", "add some chords", "add a melody", then "make it a full track".
2. Type "the melody is too loud in the drop".
Result: "Turned the melody down 5 dB, same notes." The Melody vol goes 0.96 to 0.72 for the whole song.
3. Type "make the hats softer in the break".
Result: "Drums: volume 78" (the whole drums fader).
4. Type "give the drop more energy".
Result: "Done: Groove: four-to-the-floor kick…" with no change to any note, section or setting (one undo step).
5. Type "make the drop bigger".
Result: "I couldn't turn that into a change."
Likely: src/maker.js (section words ignored by the mix and energy rules), src/actions.js (ACT.groove reply when nothing changed). assistant-dev. Per-section level would need the engine (sound-engine-dev).

text: Pan requests add or remake parts in Basic mode. "Pan the melody left" adds a new "Melody 2" track. "Put the chords a bit to the left" adds "Chords 2". "Pan the hats right" makes a new drum groove with 8th hats (124 to 94 hits). The Worker prompt has pan as a track_fx effect, but the offline parser has no pan phrase. "It sounds too dry" isn't understood either.
steps:
1. A 4-part loop (Bodzin drums, bassline, chords, melody), Loop or Song mode.
2. Type "pan the melody left".
Result: "Done: Melody 2 (new track) on Melodic Pluck." A second melody plays.
3. Type "put the chords a bit to the left".
Result: "Chords 2 (new track)".
4. Type "pan the hats right".
Result: "Done: Hi-hats: … 8th hats …", and the drum notes are rewritten.
5. Type "it sounds too dry".
Result: "I couldn't turn that into a change."
Should: track_fx pan on that track ("left" about -40, "a bit" about -20), and add reverb for "too dry". Never add a part.
Likely: src/maker.js (the mix / track_fx phrases). assistant-dev.

text: In a song, the quiet sections are as loud as the drop, or louder, so the drop doesn't hit. On a Stephan Bodzin full track, the Intro (drums only, no clap) renders at -5.8 dB RMS and the Drop (drums, bass, chords, melody) at -6.8 dB RMS, so the Intro is 1 dB louder. The Outro (drums and chords) is -6.1. On Ben Böhmer the Intro is -6.5 against the Drop's -6.4. The Short-layout MP3 measures Intro -7.9, Drop -8.1, Outro -7.9 LUFS (LRA 0.4 LU). Meanwhile the Break (pads only) drops to -25.2 dB RMS, 18 dB under the drop. The master glue and limiter push every busy section to the same ceiling. This was noted as numbers on 15 and 21 Nov (the 14 Nov "song builds energy" idea) but never filed as a bug. It matters more now that AI-1 lets people ask for a bigger drop.
steps:
1. New song: "make a beat like Stephan Bodzin", "add a bassline", "add some chords", "add a melody", then "make it a full track" (96 bars).
2. Render 4 bars from the middle of each section offline (renderSongSpan, every audible track).
Result (RMS dB / peak dBFS): Intro -5.8 / -0.7, Build -6.4 / -0.6, Drop -6.8 / -0.5, Break -25.2 / -10.0, Drop 2 -6.8 / -0.5, Outro -6.1 / -0.7.
3. Make it a short song ("make the loop 8 bars and then arrange it as a short song") and click Download MP3.
Result: ffmpeg ebur128 gives Intro -7.9, Drop -8.1, Outro -7.9 LUFS.
Should: the drop is the loudest and fullest section. An intro with fewer parts sits a few dB under it.
Likely: the master chain in renderGraph (src/studio.js ~305-312, glue plus limiter at -3 dB, ratio 20) and the same chain in live playback (src/mixer.js / src/fx.js). sound-engine-dev.

text: "Add a breakdown" puts it in the wrong place. On a plain loop, it makes a song that STARTS with a 16-bar Break: the reply is "Your song: Break 16 · Main 8", with no drums and no bass in the Break, so the first 31 seconds are pads alone. In a full track that already has a Break after the first drop, "add a breakdown after the first drop" adds a second 16-bar break right next to it. The reply, "Added Break (16 bars) before Break 2", is confusing because the new one takes the name Break and the old one becomes Break 2.
steps:
1. New song: "make a beat like Stephan Bodzin", "add a bassline", "add some chords" (4-bar loop, no layout).
2. Type "add a breakdown".
Result: sections Break 16 · Main 8. The Break comes first, with Drums and Bassline off.
3. Undo, then "make it a full track", then "add a breakdown after the first drop".
Result: Intro, Build, Drop, Break, Break 2, Drop 2, Outro (32 bars of break back to back).
Should: on a loop, Main, then Break, then Main (or ask). When a break is already there, say so and offer to make it longer.
Likely: src/maker.js ~226 and ~233 (the custom layout puts the named section before Main for anything but an outro). assistant-dev.

text: Basic mode doesn't know "make it a short song" or "make it a short track", even though the Short layout exists (Make it a song menu, and "…arrange it as a short song" works). Reply: "I couldn't turn that into a change."
steps:
1. Any 3-part loop.
2. Type "make it a short song" (or "make it a short track").
Result: "I couldn't turn that into a change."
Compare: "make the loop 8 bars and then arrange it as a short song" gives Intro 4 · Drop 8 · Outro 4.
Likely: src/maker.js:185, where the fullW regex needs "(make|turn) it (a|the) song" with nothing between them, so "a short song" never reaches SHORT_WORDS. assistant-dev.

text: "The mix is muddy" spends its cuts on a MUTED voice-note track. The reply leads with it ("…3 dB less low end on sing (150 Hz), sing → notes (308 Hz) and sing → chords (238 Hz)…"). The 308 Hz low cut lands on a melody whose lowest note is C3 (131 Hz), so it thins the melody. Seen on 21 Nov too, but not filed then.
steps:
1. "make a beat like Stephan Bodzin". Import tests/fixtures/sing.wav, then use its track menu "Turn into notes… → Bassline" (the audio is muted automatically). Then "turn the voice note into chords" and "make the voice note a melody".
2. Type "bass is muddy", then "the mix is muddy".
Result: the muted audio track "sing" gets a 150 Hz low cut and -3 dB low end, and the melody gets a 308 Hz low cut.
Should: skip muted tracks, and keep low cuts under the part's lowest note.
Likely: src/maker.js / src/actions.js (the mix-muddy rule picks the tracks). assistant-dev.

text: In Song view, the little "without" label on a drums part is cut off from the left when the section is narrow. In an 8-bar Intro with the kick taken out, the label "no clap, snare, kick" shows as "are, kick". The label sits at right:4px with nowrap and no max-width, so the start of the text is hidden.
steps:
1. A full track (Böhmer drums, bass, chords, melody), then "take the kick out of the intro" and "make it shorter" (the Intro becomes 8 bars).
2. Look at the Drums lane, Intro part.
Result: the label reads "are, kick" (screenshot shots/p2-06-after-comments.png, top left).
Should: ellipsis at the end, or a shorter label ("no kick, clap").
Likely: src/head.html:650 (.pwo needs max-width:calc(100% - 8px); overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis). studio-ux-dev.
